title: CJWasm2 Std Phase F Residual Failure Report

metadata.scope: scripts/std_test.sh L1 modules after Phases A-D

validation_backlog.notes: Representative errors are i32.wrap_i64 and i64.store stack-type mismatches.
Representative errors are i32.store operand loss, i64.and mixed-width operands, and stray i32.wrap_i64.

residual_clusters.summary: Compile compatibility is closed, but validate-only failures remain in overflow and unicode
representative_errors: type mismatch in i32.wrap_i64, expected [i64] but got [i32]
type mismatch in i64.store, expected [i32, i64] but got [i32, i32]
type mismatch in i32.store, expected [i32, i32] but got [i32]
type mismatch in i64.and, expected [i64, i64] but got [... i64, i32]
likely_root_causes: CHIR/codegen still inserts stale width-conversion operators in some Option/overflow/unicode paths
Some store operations are emitted after value-stack erosion, leaving only the pointer operand
These are validate-only codegen defects, not compile-time type inference gaps
residual_clusters.recommended_next_action: Track this as a separate validate-focused follow-up after std compatibility closure.

proposed_tail_fix_batches.title: Decompose remaining validate-only overflow/unicode backend defects

notes: Phase F reduced the non-macro compile-failure set from 31 to 0 and therefore closed the compile-compatibility portion of the std plan.
WASM validation still has 16 failures among compile-passing std files; those now form a separate validate-focused backend backlog.
The dominant next payoff remains io, not parser or generic conformance work.
scripts/std_test.sh currently names wasm outputs as mod + basename, which makes duplicate names under console/stdout and console/stderr hard to distinguish during diagnosis.
